notes: Returns whether aLinkedListNode_4295 (this node's 'next' pointer in its owning list) is non-null, i.e. whether the node is currently linked into some list. The 'if (i.toInt() != 4) return true' guard is a decoy that skips the real check unless decoy==4; ByteBufferStatics.kt calls .method2712(4.toByte()) directly to get the real answer, while the internal call from method2715 (unlink) passes 46, which is a dead/no-op invocation. Mirrors HashLinkedListNode.method3164 (a near-identical isLinked-style check one level up).

Removes this node from its current doubly-linked list by splicing its neighbors' prev/next pointers together, then nulls its own prev/next fields. Confirmed by refactor-notes/commonMain/AudioMixerScheduler.csv (method2880/detachStream) which already describes this exact method as unlinking a node from whatever list owns it; called very widely (ArchiveResourceProvider, CacheLruCache, Hashtable, LruByteCache, ImageFrameCache, ChatCommandProcessor, etc.) to remove/evict entries from intrusive linked lists such as LRU caches. decoy is a dead call-counter-only gate to method2712 further down when < 18 (never observed to matter).
